analysis: The visible changes in this batch are test-only: the modified EngineV2KVBackendGateTests.swift (changed head ranges 713-714, 720-724, 729-755) and the new EngineV2PrefillGeometryTests.swift. No production code, authorization, attestation, crypto or coordinator protocol paths are modified. The gate tests assert backend selection and prefill geometry: Gemma-4 uses the wide plain chunk, the solo stripe is nil, and the paged pool maxPrefillChunk stays at defaultSoloPrefillStripeTokens. They also assert that an explicit paged request refuses rather than silently degrading, and that the kill switch degrades. They keep the existing SSD prefix-cache coverage (T-041): HMAC-keyed layouts, an ephemeral key in tests, and PrefixCachePolicy.environmentFlag=0 disabling the cache. The tests use isolated temp roots and in-memory KEKs and never touch real keys, so no secret exposure was found. The test hermetic environment sets the guard path to /dev/null and native KV quantization, which affects only the tests. Unit 652d7b3044e122ac:0 is the new file, for which only a truncated patch excerpt was supplied, with no numbered source text. I could not inspect its full content, so I make no safety claim for it beyond the visible header and fixtures. Those fixtures are tiny random-weight models and appear benign. The production geometry change that the tests reflect (the wide prefill chunk for Gemma 4 in EngineV2Factory) was not supplied. Its availability and memory-sizing effects on the paged pool (PagedSequenceKV precondition on maxPrefillChunk, T-010/T-029 DoS class) should be reviewed in the pass that sees the Sources changes. The tests pin the pool-chunk lockstep, which reduces regression risk. No threat-model gaps were identified from these units.
